impact_pathways.impact_narrative: WP4 delivers the structured career development framework through which the fellow acquires and documents expanded scientific and transferable competences. The Career Development Plan (D4-01), co-prepared by supervisor and fellow by M3 and reviewed at M12 and M24, is the primary vehicle. WP4 tasks include a transferable-skills training programme (T4-02, ≥120 hours covering MSCA-PF mandatory dimensions) and preparation of a follow-on proposal submitted within 6 months of fellowship end. These WP4-grounded mechanisms connect directly to improved employability and career prospects within academia and beyond. impact_pathways.impact_narrative: The fellowship is an international mobility action that integrates three previously siloed methodological traditions: satellite Earth observation (Sentinel-1/2, PlanetScope), probabilistic Bayesian/machine-learning inference, and AquaCrop agronomic simulation. Working across these domains under the supervision of the host develops new interdisciplinary R&I mindsets. WP4 T4-02 delivers structured transferable-skills training; T4-03 facilitates ≥2 methods seminars at the host and ≥1 bidirectional knowledge adoption. The CDP (D4-01) plans, records, and evidences this interdisciplinary and international exposure. impact_pathways.impact_narrative: WP5 is the dedicated dissemination, exploitation, communication, and management work package. T5-01 delivers a FAIR data management plan (D5-01, M6) establishing open-data conditions for fellowship outputs. T5-03 executes targeted communication activities including conference presentations. The dissemination and exploitation report (D5-02, M24) records the full communication portfolio. These activities directly build the fellow's networking and communication capacities with scientific peers and the general public, broadening the R&I impact of the fellowship.

dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All peer-reviewed publications produced by the fellowship will be made immediately open-access upon publication, in full compliance with the Horizon Europe open-access mandate and Plan S. Preprints will be deposited on domain-appropriate open repositories (ESSOAr, arXiv, or EarthArXiv) at the point of submission to peer review. Research datasets underpinning publications will be released under CC BY 4.0 or equivalent open data licences. All fellowship software outputs will be released under an OSI-approved open-source licence. Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability (FAIR) conditions for all data and model artefacts are established in the Data Management Plan (D5-01) delivered by M6 and are maintained throughout and after the fellowship.

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: The fellowship operates at TRL 3–4 and generates primarily open scientific knowledge — peer-reviewed publications, open-source software, and FAIR data artefacts — for which open licensing is the appropriate and intended exploitation mechanism. No patent applications are anticipated for this phase of research. All software will be released under an OSI-approved open-source licence; all data under CC BY 4.0 or an equivalent permissive open data licence; all publications under immediate open-access conditions. The fellow and the host institution jointly hold publication and data rights; no third-party IP encumbrances on core fellowship outputs are foreseen. Should commercially exploitable applications emerge from the uncertainty-aware decision-support demonstrator in future funded stages, IPR management will be addressed in the follow-on proposal in accordance with the host institution's technology-transfer and knowledge-valorisation policies.

sustainability_mechanism.description: Fellowship outputs are designed for durability well beyond the M24 end date. Peer-reviewed open-access publications permanently establish the probabilistic multi-sensor crop-water estimation methodology and the uncertainty-aware decision engine in the scientific record, providing citable, independently verifiable references that persist without institutional dependency. Open-source software releases (D1-01 aligned, M14; D2-01 aligned, M20) and FAIR data artefacts governed by the DMP (D5-01, M6) ensure that the diagnostic and decision-support tools remain accessible, replicable, and extensible by the global remote sensing and precision agriculture research community under open licences. MSc co-supervision (WP4 T4-03, ≥1 thesis submitted by M24) embeds the probabilistic crop-water estimation methodology directly into the host institution's graduate curriculum, creating a durable educational pathway from fellowship research to teaching. The follow-on proposal (≥1 submitted within 6 months of M24) is the primary mechanism for continuation of the scientific programme in a subsequent funded phase at higher TRL or broader scope. The host institution, as long-term custodian of the open software repositories, FAIR data archives, and publication portfolio, sustains institutional access to and stewardship of fellowship outputs after the grant period.
